mainTopic: One act, many sets of מלקות: the furrow משנה, wearing כלאים, covering כלאים seeds, רבי עקיבא's מקיים, and whether kinds of work add up separately on יום טוב.
overview: The משנה gives a famous case: one furrow of plowing can break eight לאוין at once. חנניא בן חכינאי wants to add wearing a כלאים garment. The חכמים say that is 'not the same category,' and he answers that the נזיר item is not about plowing either. The גמרא then explains what 'taking off and putting on' כלאים means: רב אחא says a real removal is needed, while רב אשי says the time it takes is enough. רבי ינאי reports a vote that one who covers כלאים seeds with earth gets מלקות, and רבי יוחנן proves this from the furrow משנה. ריש לקיש says the proof is weak because the משנה could follow רבי עקיבא, who gives מלקות even for keeping כלאים alive, and the גמרא shows רבי עקיבא's source in a פסוק. עולא asks why sowing on יום טוב is not counted too. רבא answers that on יום טוב separate kinds of work do not add up. אביי begins a challenge to רבא from a case of cooking a גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב, and that case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: One furrow, eight prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says one furrow of plowing can make a person liable for eight לאוין, and lists the circumstances.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a person who plows one furrow and is liable for eight prohibitions: he plows with an ox and a donkey together, the animals are consecrated, he is plowing כלאים in a vineyard, it is the שביעית year, it is יום טוב, and he is both a כהן and a נזיר plowing in a place of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings an extreme case to show that a single act can carry many separate sets of מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each detail adds another לאו to the same act of plowing: the animal pair, the animals' holiness, the vineyard, the year, the day, and the person's status. Nothing is done twice; one furrow breaks them all at once.

keyTerms.meaning: A furrow, the line a plow cuts in the ground
Negative commandments (plural of לָאו), each one punishable by מלקות
Consecrated (רש"י: firstborn animals, which belong to the כהן)
Forbidden mixed plantings in a vineyard
The seventh year, when working the land is forbidden
A place of impurity, here from a dead body

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the base text for the rest of this section. Later the גמרא uses its כלאים detail to prove a new הלכה.

phrases.english: There is one who plows a single furrow
and is liable for it for eight prohibitions:
one who plows with an ox and a donkey,
and they are consecrated,
and diverse kinds in a vineyard,
and during the Sabbatical year, and on a Festival,
and he is a priest and a nazirite in a place of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ חוֹרֵשׁ תֶּלֶם אֶחָד וְחַיָּיב עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם שְׁמוֹנָה לָאוִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One act of plowing can make a person liable for eight separate לאוין.

steps.title: Adding a garment of mixed fabrics
steps.stepSummary: חנניא בן חכינאי says that if the plower is also wearing a כלאים garment, he breaks one more לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנניא בן חכינאי says: also one who is wearing כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא adds a ninth item to the list: wearing שעטנז (wool and linen) while plowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His idea is that if the list collects every לאו a person breaks while plowing, the garment he has on should count too.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who argues with the חכמים here
One who wears a garment of wool and linen mixed together

phrases.english: Ḥananya ben Ḥakhinai says:
Also one who wears diverse kinds.
phrases.notes: He means wearing a wool-and-linen garment while he plows, which would add a ninth לאו.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן חֲכִינַאי אוֹמֵר: אַף הַלּוֹבֵשׁ כִּלְאַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ninth item to the list of eight
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wearing כלאים while plowing should also be counted.

steps.title: The חכמים: wearing is a different category
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the addition, because wearing a garment has nothing to do with plowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: it is not the same category.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on חנניא בן חכינאי's addition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is supposed to contain לאוין broken by the act of plowing itself. Wearing שעטנז is a separate act that just happens at the same time, so it does not belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not the same name, meaning not the same category

phrases.english: They said to him: It is not the same category.
phrases.notes: Literally 'it is not the name.' They mean it is not a לאו that comes from plowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵינוֹ הַשֵּׁם
steps.kashyaTarget: Counting wearing כלאים in the plowing list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The list only counts לאוין connected to the act of plowing. Wearing a garment is a different act.

steps.title: The נזיר is not plowing-related either
steps.stepSummary: חנניא בן חכינאי answers that the נזיר item is not about plowing either, yet the משנה counts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: the נזיר is also not the same category.
steps.whatsHappening: חנניא בן חכינאי defends himself by turning the חכמים' own reasoning back on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר or כהן gets מלקות for being in a place of טומאה, not for plowing. If the משנה counts that, it should be willing to count the כלאים garment too.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow that forbids him, among other things, to become impure from a dead body

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the plowing itself as the נזיר's sin. His לאו comes from being in a place of טומאה, and that is exactly why חנניא בן חכינאי can say it is 'not the same category.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: אַף הַנָּזִיר לֹא הוּא הַשֵּׁם.
phrases.english: He said to them: The nazirite, too, is not the same category.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: אַף הַנָּזִיר לֹא הוּא הַשֵּׁם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turning the objection back: the list already includes an item that fails the same test
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list only counts לאוין that come from the plowing itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list already counts נזיר, which is not about plowing, so wearing כלאים can be counted too.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument is about what belongs on the list: only לאוין caused by the plowing, or every לאו broken during that act.

steps.title: What counts as taking off and putting on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'פושט ולובש' means really taking the garment off and on, or just slipping an arm in and out of the sleeve.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said in the name of רבי יוסי: 'He takes off and puts on' means really putting it on, or even just putting his arm into the sleeve of his garment and taking it out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks how much a person must do to count as a new 'wearing' of כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each new act of wearing after a warning brings another set of מלקות. The question is whether that requires fully removing and re-wearing the garment, or whether a small in-and-out of the sleeve is enough.

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai says that Rabbi Yosei says:
"He removes and dons": does it mean actually dons,
phrases.notes: This quotes the earlier משנה: someone wearing כלאים is warned, takes it off and puts it on, and is liable each time.

phrases.english: or even if he inserts and removes
the sleeve of his garment?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״פּוֹשֵׁט וְלוֹבֵשׁ״ – לוֹבֵשׁ מַמָּשׁ, אוֹ אֲפִילּוּ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a new wearing of כלאים require full removal and re-wearing, or is moving an arm in and out of the sleeve enough?

steps.title: רב אחא shows it with his hands
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא shows with a gesture that a full putting on and taking off is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא gestured: putting in and taking out.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the question by acting it out instead of saying it in words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His gesture shows really putting the garment on and taking it off. A small arm movement in the sleeve does not count as a new wearing.

phrases.aramaic: מַחְוֵי רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, gestured:
Inserting and removing.
phrases.notes: With his hands he showed fully getting into the garment and fully out of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְוֵי רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only an actual full putting on and taking off counts.

steps.title: רב אשי: just the time it takes is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says no removal is needed at all. Staying in the garment long enough to take it off and put it on makes him liable again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: even if he only stayed the amount of time it takes to take off and put on, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different way to read 'פושט ולובש': it measures time, not an action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אשי, the person does not have to move the garment at all. If, after a warning, he keeps wearing it for the length of time it would take to remove and re-wear it, that counts as a new act of wearing and brings new מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: The amount of time it takes to take off and put on

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of 'פושט ולובש': רב אחא needs a real taking off and putting on, while רב אשי counts just the time it would take.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says:
even if he only waited
the time it takes to remove and to don, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ לֹא שָׁהָה אֶלָּא כְּדֵי לִפְשׁוֹט וְלִלְבּוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading from רב אחא's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No physical removal is needed. Staying in the garment for the time it takes to take it off and put it on is enough for new liability.

steps.title: The group vote: covering mixed seeds brings lashes
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the furrow משנה, רבי ינאי reports that a group of חכמים voted that one who covers כלאים seeds with earth gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There is one who plows a furrow,' etc. רבי ינאי said: in a group they were counted and concluded: one who covers כלאים gets מלקות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the furrow משנה and brings רבי ינאי's report of a הלכה the חכמים decided by vote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that even without planting the seeds, a person who covers seeds of mixed kinds with soil is treated as sowing כלאים and gets מלקות. This needed a formal vote, which suggests it was not obvious.

phrases.english: "There is one who plows a furrow," etc.
Rabbi Yannai says:
In a group they were counted and concluded:
One who covers diverse kinds is flogged.
phrases.notes: He means covering mixed seeds with soil, which counts as sowing them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: בַּחֲבוּרָה נִמְנוּ וְגָמְרוּ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who covers כלאים seeds with earth gets מלקות.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: our משנה already says this
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks why a vote was needed and quotes the furrow משנה again, focusing on its כלאים detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to them: isn't this our משנה? 'There is one who plows one furrow and is liable for eight לאוין: one who plows with an ox and a donkey and they are consecrated, and כלאים in a vineyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן says the voted הלכה is already found in our משנה, and he re-quotes it to set up his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא really does repeat the משנה here, now for a new job: to point at the words 'כלאים בכרם.' The hint is that the vote was not needed, because a משנה already teaches the הלכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to them:
Isn't this our mishna?
There is one who plows a single furrow
and is liable for it for eight prohibitions:
one who plows with an ox and with a donkey, and they are consecrated,
and diverse kinds in a vineyard:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָאו מִשְׁנָתֵנוּ הִיא זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רבי ינאי's group needed a vote
steps.raayaObject: The הלכה that one who covers כלאים gets מלקות
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה's listing of 'כלאים בכרם' among the plowing לאוין

steps.title: Plowing breaks the mixed-seed prohibition only by covering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the proof: plowing alone is not sowing, so the משנה must mean he covers seeds as he plows.
steps.simpleTranslation: This plower who is liable for כלאים, how can you find such a case? Is it not where he covers the seeds along with his plowing as he goes?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his proof by showing the only way plowing could break the כלאים prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing is not planting, so plowing by itself should not break כלאים. The only way it fits is that the plow covers mixed seeds with soil as it moves along. So the משנה already teaches that covering כלאים brings מלקות, which is the same הלכה the group voted on.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find such a case?
Along with it as he goes

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן reads the משנה's 'כלאים בכרם' in the plowing case as covering seeds while plowing. That is a source in the משנה for the vote's ruling that covering כלאים brings מלקות.

phrases.english: This one who plows, who is liable due to diverse kinds,
how can you find such a case?
Is it not where he covers along with it as he proceeds?
phrases.notes: He means the plow covers the mixed seeds with soil as it moves along.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי חוֹרֵשׁ דְּמִחַיַּיב מִשּׁוּם כִּלְאַיִם הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the quoted משנה proves the הלכה
steps.raayaObject: One who covers כלאים gets מלקות
steps.raayaSupportSource: Plowing can only break the כלאים prohibition by covering seeds as one plows, and the משנה counts it.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: I lifted the shard, you found the pearl
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי tells רבי יוחנן that he found the proof in the משנה only because רבי ינאי first told him the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If I had not lifted the clay shard for you, would you have found the pearl underneath it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי reacts to רבי יוחנן's proof from the furrow משנה. He agrees the proof is good, but notes that he is the one who first revealed the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'shard' is the ruling רבי ינאי reported, that the חכמים voted for מלקות. The 'pearl' is the proof רבי יוחנן then found hidden in the משנה. So רבי ינאי accepts the proof and takes credit for pointing the way to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A clay shard, a broken piece of pottery

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי ינאי, answering רבי יוחנן's proof from step 10.

phrases.english: If I had not lifted the clay shard for you,
would you have found the pearl beneath it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּדַלַּאי לָךְ חַסְפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יוחנן's proof, accepting it while noting where it came from.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The proof is correct, but it was found only because רבי ינאי first stated the ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ינאי accepts that the furrow משנה proves the voted ruling, while noting that he first revealed the הלכה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the משנה may follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says he would have rejected the proof. The משנה could follow רבי עקיבא, who gives מלקות for keeping כלאים alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: If a great man had not praised you, I would have said: Whose view is our משנה? It is רבי עקיבא, who says that one who keeps כלאים growing gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש questions רבי יוחנן's proof. He says the furrow משנה could be explained another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן argued that the man in the משנה is lashed because covering seeds counts as sowing. ריש לקיש answers that, according to רבי עקיבא, he is lashed just for helping כלאים stay alive (מקיים). If so, the משנה proves nothing about covering being like sowing. He holds back only out of respect for רבי ינאי's praise.

keyTerms.meaning: One who keeps כלאים growing, even without sowing them

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not arguing about the final הלכה of the vote. He is only saying that the proof from the משנה is not airtight.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
If not for the fact that a great man praised you,
phrases.notes: The 'great man' is רבי ינאי, who just praised the proof.

phrases.english: I would have said:
Whose view is our Mishnah? It is Rabbi Akiva's,
who says: One who maintains diverse kinds is flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּקַילְּסָךְ גַּבְרָא רַבָּה, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof that רבי ינאי just praised.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוחנן's proof from the furrow משנה, not the ruling of the vote itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be explained by רבי עקיבא's view that keeping כלאים alive is punishable, so the lashes need not come from covering being like sowing.

steps.title: Where רבי עקיבא's view is found
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי עקיבא's view appears and quotes a ברייתא where he adds מקיים to weeding and covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the statement of רבי עקיבא? As a ברייתא teaches: One who weeds or covers כלאים is lashed. רבי עקיבא says: even one who maintains them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to see the source for the view ריש לקיש quoted. It brings a ברייתא that shows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gives lashes for active steps that help כלאים grow: weeding and covering with earth. רבי עקיבא goes further and adds 'one who maintains'. That is the view ריש לקיש relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: One who covers seeds with earth

phrases.english: What is the statement of Rabbi Akiva?
As it is taught: One who weeds and one who covers diverse kinds is flogged.
Rabbi Akiva says: Even one who maintains them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds the source for the view ריש לקיש used in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where is רבי עקיבא's view about מקיים כלאים taught?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא where רבי עקיבא adds 'one who maintains' to weeding and covering.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's source in the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי עקיבא learns מקיים from the wording of the פסוק about כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי עקיבא's reason? As a ברייתא teaches: 'Your field you shall not sow with כלאים.' This teaches only about sowing. Where do we learn about keeping them? The פסוק says: 'Your animals you shall not breed as כלאים; your field you shall not sow with כלאים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי עקיבא gets his idea and quotes a ברייתא that learns it from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'you shall not sow' cover only sowing. The ברייתא learns keeping כלאים from how the פסוק is written. The word כלאים comes right before 'your field', so it can be read as 'כלאים in your field', which means not letting them stay there.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, even keeping כלאים alive is forbidden by the תורה and earns מלקות. This lets ריש לקיש read the furrow משנה without saying that covering counts as sowing.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?
As it is taught: “Your field you shall not sow with diverse kinds”:
I have only one who sows;
from where do I learn one who maintains?
The verse states:
“Your animals you shall not breed as diverse kinds;
your field you shall not sow with diverse kinds.”
phrases.notes: The point is that the word כלאים sits right next to 'your field', so it can be read as 'כלאים in your field'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the view quoted in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's rule that one who maintains כלאים is lashed
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 19:19, reading the word כלאים together with 'your field'

steps.title: עולא: why not also lashes for sowing on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: עולא asks רב נחמן why the furrow משנה does not also count lashes for sowing on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to רב נחמן: Then let him also be lashed for sowing on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: עולא goes back to the furrow משנה, which lists many prohibitions broken by one act of plowing. He asks why sowing on יום טוב is missing from the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now it is assumed that covering seeds counts as sowing. If so, a man doing this on יום טוב also breaks the איסור of sowing on יום טוב. Since the משנה is listing every prohibition, that one seems to be missing.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him also be lashed

phrases.english: Ulla said to Rav Naḥman:

phrases.aramaic: וְלִילְקֵי נָמֵי מִשּׁוּם זוֹרֵעַ בְּיוֹם טוֹב!
phrases.english: And let him be flogged also for sowing on a Festival!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִילְקֵי נָמֵי מִשּׁוּם זוֹרֵעַ בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate about the proof to a new question on the list in the furrow משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of prohibitions in the furrow משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If covering seeds counts as sowing, then doing it on יום טוב also breaks the יום טוב prohibition. So the משנה should have listed it too.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the תנא left some cases out
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the תנא listed some prohibitions and left others out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The תנא taught some and left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers עולא's question. The list in the משנה was never meant to be complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן agrees that one could be lashed for sowing on יום טוב. The משנה's list just does not include every possible prohibition. So nothing is wrong with the משנה or with saying covering counts as sowing.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא taught some cases and left others out

steps.whatToRemember: A משנה's list is not always complete. תנא ושייר answers a question about a 'missing' case without changing the law.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The tanna taught and left some out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר
steps.terutzResolutionType: The list is not complete (תנא ושייר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's list seemed to include every prohibition broken in one act of plowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא left some prohibitions out, so leaving out sowing on יום טוב proves nothing.

steps.title: עולא rejects the idea that the list is incomplete
steps.stepSummary: עולא pushes back. The משנה gives an exact count of eight, so the תנא could not have left anything out.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: The תנא clearly states the number eight, and you say he listed some and left some out?!
steps.whatsHappening: עולא attacks the answer רב נחמן gave in step 16. When a משנה gives an exact number, it cannot be leaving cases out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of תנא ושייר works when a list is just examples. Here the משנה says 'eight לאוין,' an exact total. If sowing on יום טוב also counted, the total would be wrong, so we need a different reason why it was left out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He taught and left out.' The list gives some cases but is not complete.
Eight. The exact number of לאוין listed in the furrow משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: תנא ושייר is a common answer in the גמרא, but it usually does not work when the משנה gives a specific number. That is exactly the point עולא is making.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The tanna teaches 'eight,'
and you say he taught some and left some out?!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא קָתָנֵי שְׁמוֹנָה, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's answer of תנא ושייר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An exact number in the משנה means the list is complete, so nothing can have been left out.

steps.title: רבא: on יום טוב separate kinds of work do not add up
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that on יום טוב all kinds of work fall under one prohibition. Sowing adds nothing beyond the plowing that is already counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: On שבת each kind of work counts separately, but on יום טוב different kinds of work do not count separately.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to עולא's question about why sowing on יום טוב was not counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, doing several different מלאכות brings a separate liability for each one. On יום טוב there is only one prohibition against working, so plowing and sowing together bring only one punishment. The משנה already counted 'יום טוב' once for the plowing, so sowing cannot add another count.

keyTerms.meaning: Splitting of kinds of work: each type of work counts as a separate violation.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic difference between how work is counted on שבת and how it is counted on יום טוב. אביי challenges it in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava said:
There is a division of labors on Shabbat,
but there is no division of labors on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ חִילּוּק מְלָאכוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, וְאֵין חִילּוּק מְלָאכוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 17 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New legal distinction (שבת compared with יום טוב)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sowing on יום טוב should add a ninth לאו to the count.
steps.terutzMaskana: On יום טוב all work is one prohibition, so sowing adds nothing beyond the plowing already counted.

steps.title: עולא accepts רבא's answer
steps.stepSummary: עולא agrees that רבא's explanation is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: That is so.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא accepts רבא's answer, and the question about sowing on יום טוב is settled for now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this agreement, the reason the משנה left out sowing on יום טוב is that there is no separate counting of work on יום טוב. This is the position אביי will now challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is so' / 'so it shall be.' A short phrase of agreement.

phrases.english: He said to him: That is so.
phrases.notes: עולא is the one agreeing here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עָדָא תְּהֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The questioner accepts the answer given in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Sowing on יום טוב is not counted because work on יום טוב is not split into separate prohibitions.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from cooking a גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ruling that gives five sets of מלקות for cooking a גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב and eating it. This list seems to count separate kinds of work on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Is there really no division of labors on יום טוב? But we learned: One who cooks a גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב and eats it gets five sets of lashes. He is lashed for eating the גיד, for cooking on יום טוב when it is not for a permitted need, for cooking meat in milk, for eating meat and milk, and he is lashed...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a source that seems to go against רבא's rule. The list of five lashes is still being read, and its last item continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling counts 'cooking on יום טוב' as one set of lashes. The fifth item, still to come, will also be tied to doing something on יום טוב. If one act on יום טוב can bring two separate יום טוב punishments, it looks like separate kinds of work do add up on יום טוב, against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which is forbidden to eat.
Meat and milk: cooking them together and eating them are both forbidden.
Not for a permitted need. Cooking on יום טוב is allowed only for food you may eat.

steps.confusionAlert: Cooking is normally allowed on יום טוב for food. Here it is punished because the food is forbidden to eat, so the cooking does not serve a permitted need.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
And is there no division of labors on a Festival?
But didn't we learn:
One who cooks a sciatic nerve in milk on a Festival,
phrases.notes: 'גיד' here means the גיד הנשה, the nerve the תורה forbids eating (בראשית 32:33).

phrases.english: and eats it, is lashed five times.
He is lashed for eating the sciatic nerve,

phrases.aramaic: וְלוֹקֶה מִשּׁוּם מְבַשֵּׁל בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ,
phrases.english: and he is lashed for cooking on a Festival not for a permitted need,
and he is lashed for cooking the nerve in milk,
and he is lashed for eating meat in milk,
and he is lashed…

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְאֵין חִילּוּק מְלָאכוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule רבא gave in step 18, which עולא accepted in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that there is no division of labors on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known ruling counts five separate sets of lashes for one cooking-and-eating on יום טוב, including more than one count connected to יום טוב work. This suggests separate kinds of work do add up on יום טוב.
